page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an AMD EPYC 7T83 x86_64 processor clocked at 2.55 GHz. It provisions 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The memory footprint comprises 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding an allocation ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Cache hierarchy includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. The instance features no local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes, and does not include discrete GPU accelerators. Baseline network throughput is configured at 5 Gbps.

Benchmark metrics reflect strong single-core CPU throughput, with stress-ng single-core results placing in the top 25 percent at 2679.28. Multi-core performance across Geekbench (8253.0) and PassMark CPU (21196.32) remains consistently within the middle 50 percent. Text generation throughput for small language models also reaches the upper quartile at 301.48 tokens per second. A clear technical tradeoff lies in memory subsystem transfer rates: while cached 16 KB read bandwidth reaches 1028.21 GB/sec, uncached 256 MB block read bandwidth drops to 23.77 GB/sec (bottom 25 percent) and write bandwidth falls to 12.96 GB/sec (bottom 10 percent). Additionally, the processor features standard AVX, but lacks AVX-512 extensions.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides high compute density per core without the overhead of unused memory capacity or idle local disks. This resource balance makes it appropriate for compute-bound tasks with moderate RAM requirements, such as clang-based software compilation pipelines, static web serving, compression routines, and background microservice workloads.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by an AMD EPYC 7T83 x86_64 processor operating at 2.55 GHz. It provides 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores paired with 32.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The system includes 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, operates on the KVM hypervisor, and contains no local disk storage or GPU acceleration. Benchmarking highlights strong single-core performance and competitive small-model text generation speeds, balanced against average multi-core metrics. A notable constraint is its uncached memory bandwidth, which falls into the lower percentiles for large block read and write workloads. This instance profile serves compute-heavy applications such as software compilation, static web serving, compression operations, and general-purpose computational pipelines that do not depend on broad memory bandwidth or dense local storage.
